Create a figure

Source: R/basefigure.R
go_figure.Rd

A figure holds a list of traces (data) and a layout. Everything is validated against the plotly.js schema. Printing a figure renders it as an htmlwidget.

Usage

go_figure(data = NULL, layout = NULL, frames = NULL, skip_invalid = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A trace (e.g. from go_scatter()), a list of traces, or a figure (or a list with data and layout elements) to copy. Traces may be graph objects or named lists with a type element. Or a data frame: the figure starts without traces, and formula properties of later add_<trace>() calls (e.g. add_scatter(x = ~col)) are evaluated in it. The data frame is kept with the figure in R (attribute "plotly_data") but is not sent to the browser; only the values traces use are. A crosstalk::SharedData works the same way, and the traces whose points are its rows are linked to its crosstalk group (see highlight()).

layout

A go_layout() object or a named list of layout properties.

frames

Animation frames: a list of named lists with name, data (a list of traces), and optionally layout, group, traces and baseframe elements (see https://plotly.com/javascript/animations/).

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_figure object.

See also

make_subplots(), add_trace(), update_layout(), update_traces()

Examples

fig <- go_figure(
  data = go_scatter(x = 1:3, y = c(2, 1, 3)),
  layout = go_layout(title = "A figure")
)
fig <- fig |>
  add_scatter(x = 1:3, y = c(3, 2, 1), mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "x"))
if (interactive()) print(fig)

# pipe in a data frame and refer to its columns with formulas
iris |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~Sepal.Length, y = ~Sepal.Width, mode = "markers", name = "sepal") |>
  add_scatter(x = ~Petal.Length, y = ~Petal.Width, mode = "markers", name = "petal")
